statements.t: Our pipeline includes opportunities at varying stages of progression with expected award timeframes over the next 18-24 months.

We are developing Ask Airship, an agentic AI capability designed to allow users to query, analyze and act on structured data across our platform using natural language, which we intend to offer as a standalone product complementary to our Outpost AI, Acropolis, Airship Command and Fortress Server offerings.
We intend to make Ask Airship available on a software-as-a-service (subscription) basis as well as on a pay-per-use, consumption-based basis.
Ask Airship is intended to differentiate our platform from traditional video management system (“VMS”) providers.

Over time, we believe this shift could increase the proportion of our revenue that is recurring; however, it may also reduce the size of initial orders relative to our historical hardware-inclusive engagements and affect the timing of revenue recognition, and there can be no assurance that customers will adopt these purchasing models at the rate we anticipate.

For deployments in federal and other security-sensitive environments, we expect on-premises inference to rely on Western open-weight models to satisfy applicable procurement and model-origin requirements.

Our ability to execute on this strategy depends on, among other things, maintaining integrations with third-party VMS and security systems, continued availability of suitable third-party models on acceptable terms, and market acceptance of a vendor-independent architecture, and we can give no assurance that we will be successful.

During the third quarter of 2026 we significantly increased our engineering investment in Ask Airship, including expanding our dedicated development team, and we expect research and development expenses to continue to increase in the coming quarters as a result.
We currently expect to make Airship Light commercially available in the first half of 2027.

The timing of any product release, as well as market acceptance, pricing and the ultimate financial contribution of these initiatives, is subject to development, integration and competitive risks, and we can give no assurance that these initiatives will be completed on the timeline we currently anticipate or that they will generate meaningful revenue.
Separately, one of our largest commercial customers has informed us that it intends to migrate its video management operations to a different platform.

Purchases by this customer had already been declining over the past several years, and we expect the transition to occur gradually over approximately the next 12 to 18 months, during which we anticipate continuing to provide support and maintenance under our existing arrangements while revenue from this customer declines.

We do not currently expect this transition to have a material impact on our overall results of operations, but the timing and extent of the decline are outside our control, and we can give no assurance that our commercial expansion efforts will offset the associated revenue in any particular period.
We intend to use the net proceeds from the exercise of the existing warrants for working capital and general corporate purposes.
We do not believe that is reasonably certain that the lease will be extended.
To the extent that there are material differences between these estimates and our actual results, our future consolidated financial statements will be affected.
